job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

passage: Dear Diary, today I learned so much about India's space missions! My teacher explained that Mangalyaan, or the Mars Orbiter Mission, was a brilliant success. Unlike what some think, it did not carry a rover to drive on the surface, nor did it land on Mars. Instead, it was an orbiter designed to study the Martian atmosphere and surface features from space. To reach Mars, it performed complex manoeuvres, firing its engines to slow down so it could be captured by Mars's gravity. It did not just float there; gravity exists everywhere in space, and it is what keeps satellites in their orbits. Later, we discussed Aditya-L1, our mission to study the Sun. It is not going to land on the Sun, which would be impossible due to the heat. Instead, it travels to a special point called L1, where the gravitational forces of the Sun and Earth interact to allow a stable halo orbit. It takes about four months to reach this point, not just a few days. Aditya-L1 carries seven different scientific instruments to observe the Sun's corona and solar winds, proving it is much more than just a simple camera. It is amazing how ISRO achieves these feats with such precision and planning!

items.evidence: To reach Mars, it performed complex manoeuvres, firing its engines to slow down so it could be captured by Mars's gravity.
items.q: Why did Mangalyaan fire its engines as it came near Mars?
options: To slow down so Mars's gravity could capture it
To speed up so it could reach Mars faster
To hold its speed until Mars pulled it in
To aim itself straight at the surface of Mars
items.explain: Mangalyaan fired its engines to slow down, so that Mars's gravity could capture it into orbit.

wrong.why: thinks engines can only speed things up
thinks Mars pulled it in without any engine firing
thinks a spacecraft is fired straight at Mars

items.evidence: It did not just float there; gravity exists everywhere in space, and it is what keeps satellites in their orbits.
items.q: A satellite circles Earth far above the ground. What keeps it moving around Earth?
options: Earth's gravity, which reaches everywhere in space
Being so high that gravity cannot reach it
Floating freely because space has no gravity
Its engines firing all the time without stopping
items.explain: Gravity exists everywhere in space, and it is gravity that keeps satellites in their orbits.

wrong.why: thinks satellites are beyond Earth's gravity
thinks there is no gravity in space
mixes up orbiting with Mangalyaan firing its engines

items.evidence: Instead, it was an orbiter designed to study the Martian atmosphere and surface features from space.
items.q: How did Mangalyaan gather information about the planet Mars?
options: By circling Mars and observing it from above
By sending a rover to drive across it
By landing briefly to collect soil samples
By testing machines only, without doing science
items.explain: Mangalyaan was an orbiter; it studied Mars's atmosphere and surface features from space, without landing.

wrong.why: thinks it only proved technology and did no science

items.evidence: Instead, it travels to a special point called L1, where the gravitational forces of the Sun and Earth interact to allow a stable halo orbit.
items.q: What makes the point L1 a good place for Aditya-L1 to stay?
options: The Sun's and Earth's pulls allow a stable orbit
No gravity from the Sun or Earth reaches it
It gives the best view of the Moon and weather
The craft can land there on the Sun's surface
items.explain: At L1, the gravity of the Sun and Earth work together, so Aditya-L1 can keep a stable halo orbit.

wrong.why: thinks spacecraft stay up by escaping gravity
thinks Aditya-L1 studies the Moon and weather
misses that landing on the Sun is impossible

items.evidence: Aditya-L1 carries seven different scientific instruments to observe the Sun's corona and solar winds, proving it is much more than just a simple camera.
items.q: Meena says Aditya-L1 only takes photos of the Sun. Which fact shows she is wrong?
options: It has seven tools to study the corona and winds
It also studies the Moon and Earth's weather
It will land on the Sun to collect samples
It takes about four months to reach its point
items.explain: Aditya-L1 carries seven scientific instruments to observe the Sun's corona and solar winds, so it does far more than photograph.

wrong.why: thinks Aditya-L1 studies the Moon and weather
ignores that the Sun's heat makes landing impossible
picks a true detail that does not answer the question
